name: Taming Rod
summary: In Durotar, Taming Rods help novice hunters learn to command beasts. Trainers give them to students so they can practice before forming lasting bonds with animal companions.

sections.title: A Guide's Training Implement
sections.body: In Razor Hill, trainers such as Thotar give Taming Rods to aspiring orc and troll hunters. These enchanted tools help novices who cannot yet bind a wild creature permanently. A rod pacifies a regional predator, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid, so the hunter can practice giving commands and fighting beside an animal companion. The bond lasts only briefly, leaving the student free to learn without forming a lasting tie to the beast.

sections.title: A Step Toward Mastery
sections.body: Each Taming Rod's magic fades after a short while, and each is attuned to specific kinds of wild beasts. Novices face successive trials against different temperaments, from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters. When a student has shown they can command them, the rod goes back to the trainer. The trainer then teaches the student to tame, call, and dismiss lifelong companions without an artifact.

faq.q: What is a Taming Rod used for?
aliases: why do i have a taming rod
faq.answer: Hunters use a Taming Rod to practice commanding a beast in battle. The trainer gives it to a young hunter, and its magic briefly pacifies and charms the creature.

faq.q: Do I keep the pet I tame with the rod?
faq.answer: No. A beast under a Taming Rod's influence is there only for training, and the bond ends when the magic fades or you return the rod. After your trials, you learn to tame a lasting companion.

faq.q: Can I use any Taming Rod on any animal?
aliases: does the rod work on anything
faq.answer: No. Each Taming Rod is attuned to a specific target creature for its stage of training, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid.

faq.q: Can I keep the Taming Rod after completing the training?
faq.answer: No. You return the Taming Rod to your hunter trainer after your assignment. After your final trial, the trainer teaches you to tame, summon, and dismiss beasts on your own.

angles.text: As a hunter, you use the Taming Rod to practice before you can form lasting bonds with wild beasts.
In Durotar and Mulgore, trainers such as Thotar use Taming Rods to test whether young recruits have the discipline to master Kalimdor's harsh wildlife.
